text: The policeman on the beat. <break time="0.8s" /> Moved up the avenue impressively. <break time="0.8s" /> It was his habit. <break time="0.8s" /> Not a show. <break time="0.8s" /> Because there were few people. <break time="0.8s" /> To see him. <break time="0.8s" /> The time was barely ten oclock at night. <break time="0.8s" /> But the streets were almost empty. <break time="0.8s" /> Chilly gusts of wind. <break time="0.8s" /> With a taste of rain. <break time="0.8s" /> Had driven people indoors. <break time="0.8s" /> He tried doors. <break time="0.8s" /> As he walked. <break time="0.8s" /> Twirling his club. <break time="0.8s" /> With many skillful movements. <break time="0.8s" /> Now and then he looked down the quiet street. <break time="0.8s" /> With a careful eye. <break time="0.8s" /> This was a part of town. <break time="0.8s" /> That went to bed early. <break time="0.8s" /> Here and there. <break time="0.8s" /> A cigar store or an all night lunch counter. <break time="0.8s" /> Still had lights on. <break time="0.8s" /> Most of the doors belonged. <break time="0.8s" /> To shops. <break time="0.8s" /> Which had closed hours earlier. <break time="0.8s" /> In the middle of a block. <break time="0.8s" /> The policeman suddenly slowed down. <break time="0.8s" /> In the doorway. <break time="0.8s" /> Of a dark hardware store. <break time="0.8s" /> A man was leaning. <break time="0.8s" /> With an unlighted cigar in his mouth. <break time="0.8s" /> It is all right, officer. <break time="0.8s" /> He said quickly. <break time="0.8s" /> I am just waiting for a friend.
